summary: Red Dust Outpost is an educational space exploration and survival game that challenges players to build, manage, and sustain outposts across the solar system. Through resource management, spacecraft exploration, construction, and mission-based challenges, players experience the realities of surviving beyond Earth. Inspired by NASA data and featuring over 200 3D models of real spacecraft, rovers, and astronaut equipment, the game combines strategy, survival, and STEM education to develop the next generation of space explorers.

Project Details: Red Dust Outpost
Red Dust Outpost is an interactive space exploration and strategy game that allows players to experience the challenges and possibilities of humanity expanding beyond Earth. The game features three main modes: Story Mode (BUILD), Moon Survival (SURVIVE), and Adventure: The Grand Tour (EXPLORE).
1. What does it do or how does it work?
The game allows players to take on different space missions through three gameplay modes. In Story Mode, players construct and defend outposts across different celestial bodies while managing resources, researching upgrades, and completing missions. In Moon Survival, players experience life on the lunar surface by gathering supplies, building habitats, and managing essential survival resources while facing environmental hazards. In Adventure: The Grand Tour, players pilot spacecraft and explore destinations throughout the solar system, complete missions, and interact with 3D models of real space technology.
Players can also scan objects, discover scientific information, and complete educational activities throughout their journey.
2. What benefits does it have?
Red Dust Outpost combines entertainment with education. It introduces players to space science, planetary environments, space technology, and the challenges of human exploration. It also encourages critical thinking, decision-making, resource management, and problem-solving through interactive gameplay. By making scientific concepts part of the experience, the game makes learning about space more engaging and accessible.
3. What is the intended impact of the project?
The project aims to inspire curiosity about the universe and encourage interest in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM). It hopes to help players better understand the challenges of space exploration while inspiring the next generation to appreciate scientific discovery and consider future possibilities in space science and exploration.
4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?
The project was developed as a browser-based game using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with Three.js for 3D graphics and interactive environments. We also used NASA's 3D Resources to incorporate models of real spacecraft, rovers, and astronaut equipment. Development involved computers, web browsers, code editors, and testing tools to build, improve, and test the game.
5. How is your project creative?
Our project creatively combines three different space experiences into one game: outpost construction and defense, lunar survival, and solar system exploration. Instead of simply presenting facts about space, it allows players to interact with environments, operate spacecraft, build settlements, scan objects, and discover scientific information through gameplay. It also features voice acting recorded by our team, multiple language options, and interactive 3D environments to make the experience more immersive.
6. What factors did your team consider?
Our team considered educational value, gameplay experience, scientific accuracy, accessibility, and technical limitations. We aimed to make the game enjoyable while keeping its space-related information connected to real science and NASA resources. We also considered different player devices by providing phone and laptop/desktop interface options, as well as multiple language options to make the game more accessible. Most importantly, we considered how to balance entertainment and learning so that players could enjoy the game while gaining a better understanding of space exploration.
